entities.summary:
Demosthenes was a Greek statesman and orator in ancient Athens (431–321 BCE) who played a crucial role in Athenian politics during the Peloponnesian War. He delivered his first judicial speeches at the age of 20, successfully arguing that he should gain from his guardians what was left of his inheritance.

Demosthenes' orations constitute a significant expression of contemporary Athenian intellectual prowess and provide insight into the politics and culture of ancient Greece during the 4th century BC. His most famous speeches include 'Against Meidias,' 'Against Timocrates,' and 'On the Crown.'

Despite his influential speeches, Demosthenes' personal life remains somewhat of a mystery, with details about his family, relationships, and later years remaining uncertain.

Demosthenes was known for his impassioned oratory skills, using rhetorical devices to engage his audience and make complex ideas accessible. His legacy extends beyond ancient Greece, influencing Western oratory and political discourse.
